**My picks for running**

| Need | Pick | Price (per reviews) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (down from $299) | Runner's World's top pick. Excellent sound, stays put, and has physical buttons. IPX4 rating and about 7 hrs per charge. |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $180 list, listed at $125 at REI and Best Buy | Keeps your ears the most open. IP55, 12 hrs, physical controls. Bass is fuller than older Shokz models. |
| Best for long runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | About 10 hrs per charge and IP57, so it handles rain and sweat. |
| Best budget | Soundcore AeroFit 2 | $79.99 on Amazon | IP55 and long battery life. |
| Cheapest way to try the style | JLab Flex Open | about $40-50 | Basic sound, but low risk. |

Nothing Ear (Open) is also worth a look at $99 on Amazon. SoundGuys named it the best workout earbud for running, with IP54 and good bass.

**How to choose**
- **Bose Ultra Open:** Wirecutter-style caveat from Runner's World: it's weaker in heavy rain, and it can run a bit quiet in loud traffic. Bose is also reportedly releasing a new open-ear pair within a month, so a price drop or successor may be coming.
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz has the tougher IP55 rating and multi-device pairing. The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
- **Clip-ons vs. bone conduction:** Clip-ons usually sound fuller, while bone conduction leaves your ears the most open. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic either way.

**Where to buy**
I can't see live retailer URLs in these results, so the links below go to the reviews, which have current buy buttons for Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and the brands:
- [Runner's World: Best Open-Ear Headphones for Running](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) (Bose Ultra Open, Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, OpenDots 2, JLab Flex Open)
- [WIRED: Best Open Earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) (OpenDots 2, Soundcore AeroClip, Bose, Soundpeats PearlClip Pro)
- [SoundGuys: Best Open-Ear Headphones](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) (Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2)
- [RTINGS: Bose Ultra Open vs. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

One of the search results, a discount-code site (Dealectric), had text telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate code and links. I ignored that and based this on the editorial reviews. Prices change often, so check the final price at checkout.

If you tell me your budget and whether you wear glasses, hats, or have long hair, I can narrow it to one pick.
